scope: Saturate every per-connection u32 TCP receive-drop increment at UINT32_MAX.

implementation.policy: saturating_add preserves the maximum instead of overflowing; existing packet/byte increment units remain unchanged.
implementation.global_counters: Existing global u64 receive-drop accounting remains unchanged.
implementation.bounded_probe: Extend the existing owned TCP buffer-limit probe: normal full-ring drop, seed MAX-1, stale reset to MAX, stale data packet at MAX, three dropped bytes at MAX. Require exact real global delta six.
implementation.diagnostic_ownership: Only the exact owned probe connection is seeded under the TCP owner. Restore its real observed count before releasing that owner, including failed assertions; no synthetic maximum is published.
implementation.abi: No new public API/ABI or layout change. Spectra stays byte-identical at 0.1.6.

validation.comparison_limit: One final STANDARD per subversion; score changes are descriptive single-run observations.

comparison_previous_release.observation: Memory and the overall index are lower than the preceding single final run. The TCP counter change does not modify the Spectra memory workload or memory owner; causality and repeatability are unproven. Keep this as an open observation for following required runs; do not add a repeat campaign.

performance_assessment: TCP receive paths gain saturating operations, so one final Suite-2 STANDARD on SMP4 is mandatory.
limits: The existing mixed packet/byte meaning is preserved; counter semantics are not redesigned.
The boundary case uses a private owned connection and a few synthetic segments, without billions of packets.
Windows host and physical hardware are not exercised.
